title: A Tryouts for the Detention
premise: Petra Dunmore, a debate champion whose home life is a losing argument, is dragged into a mysterious group chat called 'The Tryouts' that predicts events in the town of Halloway before they happen. The chat's messages trace back to the Founders' Trial, a century-old tradition that quietly holds the town's timeline together—and it's unraveling. As Petra and four other 'tryouts' race to complete the Trial's forgotten final round, he discovers his own family's role in breaking it generations ago. In the end, Petra must choose between restoring the tradition (and erasing the memories of everyone he's come to love) or letting time collapse around them—and he finds a third way: rewriting the Trial so memory becomes its foundation instead of its casualty.
about_author: Ansel Ishikawa grew up in a small river town where every festival felt older than the buildings housing it, an obsession that never quite wore off. A former high-school debater who lost more arguments than he won, he writes about kids who are fine—obviously.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He wins the regional debate semifinal, then comes home to his parents' cold war and performs 'fine' flawlessly for both sides. Establishes his habit of arguing to avoid feeling. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A chat titled 'A Tryouts for the Detention' appears on his phone with six members, none of whom added each other. The first message predicts tomorrow's fire drill—down to the minute. Beat: unease disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Five Strangers, One Thread
chapters.summary: Petra tracks down the other members: Marisol, Dev, June, and Theo, each from a different clique. They compare screenshots; all predictions have come true. POV alternates briefly via their chat logs. Beat: reluctant alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Prediction That Wasn't Small
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The chat predicts the collapse of the bell tower at Halloway High—three days out. No one believes it until cracks appear overnight. Beat: dread replacing novelty; stakes become physical.

chapters.title: Detention as Doorway
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The five get detention together (the chat's title finally makes sense) and find the 1904 Founders' Trial records sealed in the old detention room wall. Beat: discovery—the tradition that made the town was a test, not a celebration.

chapters.title: What the Trial Actually Was
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Research montage: every generation, five students were 'tried' to renew the town's founding covenant; the last Trial in 1974 ended incomplete. Since then, predictions leak through the cracks. Beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: My Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He finds his mother's name in the 1974 trial roster—she was one of the five who walked away. Their first honest conversation in years ends in a slammed door. Beat: betrayal; the argument he can't win.

chapters.title: June Sees It First
chapters.summary: June's POV. June, who has synesthesia-like sensitivity to the chat, realizes the predictions are getting closer together—time is fraying faster. She hides a prediction about herself. Beat: fear and isolation inside the group.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Terrified, Theo leaks the Trial to the principal, hoping adults will fix it. Instead the records vanish and the chat goes silent for two days. Beat: the cost of handing power back to authority.

chapters.title: Silence Is Louder
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. With no predictions, the tower holds—but small things vanish: a street, a classmate's name from yearbooks. Petra realizes erasure, not explosion, is how the timeline dies. Beat: quiet horror.

chapters.title: The Round That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The five decode the Trial's structure: three rounds were held publicly; a fourth, secret round was always required and always skipped. The chat is the fourth round trying to assemble itself. Beat: hope—the rules can be met.

chapters.title: Practice Arguments
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The group rehearses the Trial like a debate case, and Petra teaches them his craft while learning theirs. Warm interlude; Petra and June grow close. Beat: found-family tenderness before the fall.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Full-group scene, rotating close-third. They attempt the fourth round at the tower; it fails because the covenant demands something each of them refuses to give up—a memory. Beat: first real defeat.

chapters.title: What Memory Costs
chapters.summary: June's POV. June reveals her hidden prediction: completing the Trial erases the participants' memories of each other. Love against duty crystallizes. Petra and June's almost-something gets a deadline. Beat: heartbreak with a countdown.

chapters.title: Mother's Confession
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. His mother finally explains 1974: she refused to forget her brother, who'd died that spring, and walked out—dooming the cycle. She chose love too, and has regretted the town ever since. Beat: empathy replacing anger; generational echo.

chapters.title: The Town Notices
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Erasure accelerates—roads loop, parents repeat conversations. The five must choose: complete the Trial now or lose the raw material of themselves. Theo wants out; Marisol refuses to let him go alone. Beat: fracture and loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Rebuttal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra does what he does best—he argues, this time with the covenant itself, cross-examining the Trial's logic in the chat until the rules respond with a loophole: a fifth option no generation ever tried. Beat: his debate skill becomes salvation.

chapters.title: The Fifth Option
chapters.summary: Group scene. The loophole: offer memories willingly to be held, not erased—make remembering the Trial's act of renewal. But it requires all five, including Theo, and it's never been done. Beat: terrified consensus.

chapters.title: Trial by Night
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. At the cracking tower, the five perform the rewritten fourth round as the town's missing pieces rain back into place. Each must speak a memory aloud and mean keeping it. Beat: sacrifice transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Held Breath
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Dawn. The tower stands; the chat sends one final message—'Tryouts complete'—and dissolves. The five remember everything, which is its own strange grief and gift. Beat: exhausted relief.

chapters.title: The Argument at Home
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Armed with his mother's story, Petra wins the argument at home—not by debating, but by listening. His parents begin talking to each other again. Beat: the private victory mirroring the public one.

chapters.title: Fine, Actually
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, epilogue tone. Months later: the five meet weekly, officially a 'debate club.' Petra and June sit close. When a new unknown number texts a single prediction, they all smile instead of flinching. Beat: identity chosen, memory kept, love against duty resolved.
